title: Module kernel from a functorial family of enlarged-site singleton covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use sites small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C_X$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X$ be the enlarged etale ringed site and extended structure sheaf of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and let $M$ be a sheaf of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $W,Z:Y_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal C_X$ are functors and $c:Z\to W$ is natural, with every singleton $Z(V)\to W(V)$ a covering [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $Q(V)=Z(V)\times_{W(V)}Z(V)$ with its two projections, functorially in $V$. Suppose given natural ring maps $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X(W(V))$. Use their composites with ring restrictions to give $M(W(V)),M(Z(V)),M(Q(V))$ their $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-module structures, and assume these three presheaves are sheaves; denote them $H_W,H_Z,H_Q$. Then restriction gives morphisms $i:H_W\to H_Z$ and $d_1,d_2:H_Z\to H_Q$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaves, and $i$ induces a canonical isomorphism $H_W\simeq\ker(d_1-d_2)$. On every $V$, restriction is injective and its image consists exactly of the sections of $M(Z(V))$ having equal restrictions to $Q(V)$. The inverse on this kernel assigns the unique antecedent in $M(W(V))$; it is linear and commutes with restriction in $V$ and with morphisms in $M$. Thus $0\to H_W\to H_Z\xrightarrow{d_1-d_2}H_Q$ is exact at the first two terms, with no assertion of surjectivity at $H_Q$.

proof.text: Write $r_V=M(c_V)$ and $p_{j,V}:Q(V)\to Z(V)$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restrictions are additive and semilinear. If $\alpha_V:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X(W(V))$ is the given map, then $r_V(\alpha_V(a)x)=\alpha_V(a)|_{Z(V)}r_V(x)$. Thus $r_V$ is $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear. Also $c_Vp_{1,V}=c_Vp_{2,V}$, so either route defines the same scalar action on $M(Q(V))$, and both $M(p_{j,V})$ are linear. Naturality of $c$ and of the pullback projections makes these maps commute with restriction in $V$. The natural ring maps give the scalar compatibility for these restrictions. Since the three presheaves are assumed sheaves, these are the required module-sheaf morphisms $i,d_1,d_2$.

source.place: Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules), semilinear restrictions and morphisms; Tag 03M8 of spaces-morphisms.tex, final functoriality sentence.

proof.text: Work in the enlarged ringed site in the hypotheses, with its specified singleton covers and pullbacks. The underlying abelian presheaf of $M$ is a sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By the definition of an abelian sheaf on a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ the diagram $M(U)\to\prod_iM(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}M(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer; the fibre products exist by axiom (iii) of that definition. Apply this to the singleton covering $c_V:Z(V)\to W(V)$, for each $V$. Its only overlap is $Q(V)=Z(V)\times_{W(V)}Z(V)$, and the two maps are $M(p_{1,V})$ and $M(p_{2,V})$. Therefore $r_V$ is injective, its image is exactly $\{z:M(p_{1,V})(z)=M(p_{2,V})(z)\}$, and every such $z$ has a unique antecedent $s_V(z)$ in $M(W(V))$.

Put $K_V=\{z:(d_{1,V}-d_{2,V})(z)=0\}$. Equality of the two images is equivalent to their difference being zero. Linearity from step 1 makes $K_V$ a submodule. For $z,z\prime\in K_V$ and $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $r_V(s_V(z)+s_V(z\prime))=z+z\prime$, $r_V(a s_V(z))=az$, and $r_V(0)=0$. Uniqueness in step 2 gives $s_V(z+z\prime)=s_V(z)+s_V(z\prime)$, $s_V(az)=a s_V(z)$ and $s_V(0)=0$. Hence $r_V:M(W(V))\to K_V$ and $s_V$ are inverse linear maps.

proof.text: For $h:V\prime\to V$ and $z\in K_V$, naturality of $d_1,d_2$ puts $z|_{Z(V\prime)}$ in $K_{V\prime}$. The naturality square for $c$ gives $r_{V\prime}(s_V(z)|_{W(V\prime)})=z|_{Z(V\prime)}$, so uniqueness gives $s_V(z)|_{W(V\prime)}=s_{V\prime}(z|_{Z(V\prime)})$. For a module-sheaf morphism $\theta:M\to N$ to another module satisfying the same sheaf assumptions, its naturality gives $r_V^N(\theta_{W(V)}s_V^M(z))=\theta_{Z(V)}(z)$. This lies in $K_V^N$, and uniqueness gives $\theta_{W(V)}s_V^M(z)=s_V^N(\theta_{Z(V)}z)$. Thus the inverse commutes with both kinds of restriction claimed.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), final functoriality sentence; uniqueness checks expanded.

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the sheaf kernel $K=\ker(d_1-d_2)$ is computed sectionwise, so $K(V)=K_V$ with the induced restrictions. Steps 3 and 4 assemble the inverse maps into a module-sheaf morphism $s:K\to H_W$. The factored map $i:H_W\to K$ satisfies $si=1$ and $is=1$ on every section, hence is a canonical isomorphism. The inclusion $K\to H_Z$ is the kernel of $d_1-d_2$; consequently $i$ is monic and identifies $H_W$ with that kernel, which is exactly the asserted exactness at $H_W$ and $H_Z$. Nothing here requires the last map to be surjective.
